name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,245

clue.text: Reduction of tension once sail date is rearranged

indicators.note: things rearranged are put into a different order, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: three words taken as written, twelve letters in all

explanation.surface: A sailing has been rescheduled, and the change of date eases everyone's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first three words; everything after it is the fodder plus its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: When a conflict or standoff is calmed down step by step, diplomats call the process this, a lowering of hostility.

clue.text: Teach Early English, introducing coin of past

indicators.note: to introduce is to bring something inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: EE is the standard abbreviation for the Early English style of architecture
a ducat was a gold coin used across Europe in earlier centuries

explanation.surface: A history teacher works an old coin into a lesson on early English.
explanation.walkthrough: Early English reads as the subject being taught, but it is just two letters, split apart to hold the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to instruct someone, passing on knowledge through lessons or training.

clue.text: Bus isn’t out — it’s in need of repair — changes made

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken and jumbled, so the letters must be put back into working order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A broken-down bus can't go out on its route, so the timetable has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like an anagram signal, but it belongs to the fodder; the real signal is 'in need of repair'.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping one person or thing for another, as a coach does with players, counts as making replacements, so the plural fits.

clue.text: Taking part in trials, a certain European region

indicators.note: something taking part in an event sits inside it, so the letters are found within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone is entering trials, perhaps sporting or legal, held somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma and spaces are ignored when reading the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a historic area of northeastern France bordering Germany, famous for its white wines.

clue.text: Important changes with open distribution of share

indicators.note: a verb of alteration here, telling the solver the letters must be altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company announces major reforms alongside a public share offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' reads as a noun in the surface, but it is the verb signalling the anagram of the words either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dividing something up and allotting each party its portion is the act this noun names.

clue.text: Bungling at home, starts to embarrass people totally

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: someone at home is said to be in
the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A clumsy person at home keeps causing total embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: IN for 'at home' is a common crossword equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe someone clumsy and lacking skill, doing things badly.

clue.text: Not sharp or flat, as is to be expected

blocks.note: first meaning: in music, a note neither raised nor lowered
second meaning: normal, unsurprising

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' and 'flat' look like descriptions of a blade or a surface, but they are musical terms.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the sign cancelling a sharp or flat bears this name; in ordinary speech it means normal or predictable.

clue.text: Worn American media boss

blocks.note: US is the standard abbreviation for American
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper or magazine

explanation.surface: A tired-looking executive running an American media company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn' seems to describe the boss, but it is the definition standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are secondhand or showing wear from earlier owners are described with both adjectives.

clue.text: Firework question interrupting sibling

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into something, so one piece is placed in the middle of another

blocks.note: sib is a short form of sibling
QU is a standard abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A child keeps butting in with questions about fireworks while a brother or sister talks.
explanation.walkthrough: The blocks are listed outer piece first, then the piece that goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small firework that hisses before exploding, as in the phrase damp squib.

clue.text: Fool that is not disheartened or wise

indicators.note: to lose heart is to lose the centre, so the middle letter of a word is removed

blocks.note: a sap is a gullible, foolish person
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, meaning that is
taken as written before its middle letter goes

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a person is a fool or a sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' with its central O removed leaves NT. 'Or' joins the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe someone with deep knowledge and sound judgement, the former being a more literary word.

clue.text: Severe part of dialectic: it’s arduous, in retrospect

indicators.note: a part of something lies within it, so the letters come from inside the words
looking in retrospect means looking backwards, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A philosophy student, looking back, finds that a part of the dialectic course was harsh going.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon and apostrophe are ignored when reading the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Measures taken that are extreme and forceful in effect are described by both adjectives.

clue.text: Device with blades, reversible

indicators.note: something reversible can be turned back to front and stay the same, so the word reads identically both ways

blocks.note: the spinning part of a helicopter or turbine, which carries blades

explanation.surface: A reversible fan with blades that can spin either way.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no wordplay beyond the hint that the answer reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating assembly of a helicopter, turbine or fan carries several vanes, which suits the description.

clue.text: Rest as site redeveloped

indicators.note: a redeveloped area is rebuilt in a new layout, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Building work halts while a construction site is redeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' could be the remainder of something, but here it means a pause for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an afternoon nap taken in hot countries, a specific kind of break or sleep.

clue.text: Son, with sign of hesitation, promises to pay — not joking!

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
er is the sound people make when hesitating
an IOU (I owe you) is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A son hesitantly hands over IOUs and insists he means it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits after the dash, a common place to tuck it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sincere and earnest rather than teasing is described this way, a straightforward synonym phrase.

clue.text: Gun shop is to license guards

indicators.note: to guard is to keep something safely inside, so the letters are held within the words

blocks.note: the run starts at the end of the first word and finishes at the start of the last

explanation.surface: A gun shop is applying for a licence to have security guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun shop' looks like one phrase, but 'Gun' alone is the definition. 'License' is the North American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A small firearm held and fired with one hand is a specific kind of firearm.

clue.text: Expert leaving device to measure angles in farm vehicle

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
the semicircular instrument used in geometry to measure angles

explanation.surface: An expert leaves a geometry tool behind in a farm vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first three letters of the geometry instrument leaves the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the powerful engine-driven machine farmers use to pull ploughs and trailers across fields.

clue.text: Purchased land unfortunately knocked America to begin with

indicators.note: what comes to begin with is at the start, so only opening letters are kept

blocks.note: alas is an exclamation of regret, used when something is unfortunate
the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A buyer regrets a land deal that hurt America.
explanation.walkthrough: The United States bought this territory from Russia in 1867, which is why it is called purchased land.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1867 deal with Russia, once mocked as Seward's Folly, transferred this northern territory to the United States for cash.

clue.text: Suitable punch

blocks.note: first meaning: proper, appropriate
second meaning: a boxing blow named after the hand that throws it

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a fitting drink, but they are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fitting or correct, and in boxing it is a blow delivered with the stronger hand.

clue.text: One at wedding maybe judged correctly, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the answer is spelt differently from the word it sounds like

blocks.note: to have guessed right is to have judged correctly

explanation.surface: Someone at a wedding correctly predicts how things will turn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the wedding as one example of where such a person is found.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone invited to attend a wedding reception is an invitee, one example of the broader word.

clue.text: Stock policy ahead of time

blocks.note: a line is a stated policy, as in the party line
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A rule about stock-keeping that runs ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' suggests shares or goods, but here it means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's ancestry or descent from a family line is called their stock, as in coming from good stock.

clue.text: Merit attention? Not at first

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening, so only the initial letter is kept

blocks.note: to lend an ear is to give attention
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a matter deserves notice and answers no, not yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' sounds like a reply to the question, but it gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve a reward through effort is to gain it by right, so both verbs work.

clue.text: Responsibility to include euro — you missed out — very demanding

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other
something missed out is omitted, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: an onus is a burden or duty
taken as written
U sounds like you, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A burden involving the euro that you have been excused from proves very tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You missed out' acts on the euro alone, so drop its U before putting what is left inside the burden word.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that is burdensome and hard to carry out is described by both, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Record one making regular payment starting late

indicators.note: something starting late misses its beginning, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: a tenant pays rent on a regular schedule

explanation.surface: A clerk logs someone who pays regularly but began late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to write down.
explanation.definitionFit: To write data into a ledger or log is to put it in, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Elite troops admitting note works all right

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, the British special forces regiment
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a works is an industrial plant

explanation.surface: Special forces let a memo through, and the plant is running smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is the British Army's special forces regiment. 'Works' is a noun here, a manufacturing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acceptable and adequate, meeting the required standard, can be called okay or fine.
